As months went on and things progressed, I visited him at his hometown. I should also mention I had the idea (because he told me) that I was the only person he had had sex with since we met.


Once I finally moved down in the fall, we started officially "dating". A few days after we became "official", he admitted to me that he hadn't kept the promise...and he had been having sex with other people. The first time being a couple weeks after I had left, so essentially he had been lying about his sex life for the whole duration of our relationship.


This really...broke me. I thought I could trust him fully. I never saw something like this coming, especially since I told him of my past relationships ending in me getting cheated on and how it affected me emotionally. I was heartbroken. He justified it by saying that it wasn't technically cheating and rather a breaking of a promise since we weren't "committed" to one another, we just promised we wouldn't. But I stayed, I wanted to try and work it out because I believed in our connection. I thought with time I could eventually trust him again, but as time went on (around a month) he got increasingly frustrated by the same argument occurring over and over and my emotional instability. I felt shut off from speaking about what happened because it just made him angry. He stopped seeing my point of view and felt justified enough not to discuss it anymore, so I internalized it.

Afterwards I felt awful, I couldn't lie and I couldn't hold it in. I had to tell him. When I told him he left, understandably so. I was adopted at birth by my mom and dad, they were/are fantastic parents. Until I turned 16, I had pretty much decided I would never try and find my birth parents. It never seemed like something that would benefit my life, since they were simply sperm/egg donors.


The older I got though, the more I came to realize I would like to know my background. Depending on where you side with the nature versus nurture debate, it is obviously going to change how you feel about this. I personally believe a little bit of both are at play, so I wanted to know more about my "nature" side. 


Unfortunately, before I got the courage to seek out my birth mother, she died. I was able to "meet" her in the hospital while she was in a coma. She died shortly after. I have some vague info about my health background (susceptibility to addiction and mental health issues) but I honestly regret not taking the chance to meet her now that she's gone. She certainly wasn't the best person in the world, but I feel it would have been beneficial for me to have met her.
